info.title: axle Showcase API
info.description:
Every route here is real. The handlers parse what the spec says they accept
and send what it says they return, so you can try each one from Swagger UI.

Start with **Media** for content types, **Headers** for conditional requests
and rate limits, **Parameters** for how arrays and objects travel in a URL,
**Security** for every scheme type, and **Schemas** for unions and generics.

Demo credentials: API key `demo-key`, bearer token `demo-token`, basic auth
`demo` / `demo`.

servers.description: Local, if you started the server with `PORT=9090`.

tags.name: Media
tags.description: Content types in and out, from JSON and XML to PNG, PDF, and streams.

tags.name: Headers

tags.name: Parameters

tags.name: Security
tags.description: One route for every kind of security scheme.

tags.name: Schemas

tags.name: Responses
tags.description: Status codes, ranges, redirects, and problem details.

post.description: Send the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body and you get the original response back with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The same key with a different body is a `409`.

get.summary: Every way to send arrays and objects in a query string
get.description:
| Parameter | Style | Looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tags` | `form`, exploded | `tags=a&tags=b` |
| `ids` | `form`, not exploded | `ids=1,2,3` |
| `sort` | `pipeDelimited` | `sort=name|price` |
| `fields` | `spaceDelimited` | `fields=a%20b` |
| `filter` | `deepObject` | `filter[color]=red&filter[minSize]=2` |

The response shows what the server parsed.

parameters.description: Free text, with two named examples.

parameters.description: Repeat the parameter: `tags=a&tags=b`.

get.description: Each poll moves the job along; the third one finds it done.

Try `200`, `201`, `204`, `301`, `302`, `304`, `404`, `418`, `429`, or `503`. Redirects carry a `Location`; `429` and `503` carry `Retry-After`. A code that is not listed here still works and falls under the `2XX`, `3XX`, `4XX`, `5XX`, or `default` response, so the spec describes it.

get.summary: anyOf: match one schema or several
get.description: `?kind=email`, `?kind=phone`, or `?kind=both`. Unlike `oneOf`, a value may satisfy more than one schema, which is why `both` is valid.

get.summary: A model with a field of every type
get.description: Integers, floats, booleans, strings, dates, durations, URIs, big numbers, bytes, enums, lists, sets, maps, nested and nullable objects, and every constraint keyword.
The keys are SKUs; the schema uses `additionalProperties`.
`Manager` is `allOf` `Employee`, which is `allOf` `Person`. Each level lists only the fields it adds.
